summary: Bound evidence-log pending expiry work and checkpoint fresh signing results first

replay.detail: A pull rechecks at most 500 expired pending names, oldest first, after checkpointing new records. Pending names are released only after their signed checkpoint succeeds, so an interruption cannot accumulate another uncheckpointed expiry batch. An exact verified copy already active after the last GC line finishes interrupted cleanup without verification again; retired copies take the full check.

schema.detail: Evidence records, signed log lines and the local name-to-unix-time pending mapping retain their formats. A rejected expiry attempt renews its pending timestamp.

rules.detail: The 24-hour pending lifetime now admits at most 500 rechecks per pull. Rejected names remain pending and wait another 24 hours rather than blocking older work. Record acceptance, signer trust, GC retention and guarded log publication are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: No new CLI flags or wire fields. Existing pending files are readable without migration. Exact-object copy reuse follows the existing acceptance rule; pending state never substitutes for signature verification.

downtime.detail: No restart or deadline increase. At a two-minute cadence, 20,000 expired valid names need 40 successful pulls, about 80 minutes after becoming eligible. Fresh records are checkpointed before expiry work.

manual.detail: Install the updated evidence-log tool through the normal operations process. Keep paused GC paused until all recovery fixes are installed and an operator explicitly releases the pause. No installed state or service is changed by this code update.

recovery.detail: A killed or refused checkpoint leaves pending names held; the next pull selects the oldest names again. A checkpointed verified copy can finish pending cleanup after interruption. Remote-absent names are pruned immediately. With no further GC runs, pending state cannot grow, and valid names drain in bounded batches; rejected names remain bounded by the existing pending set. Reverting restores mass expiry, so drain a large eligible backlog before reverting.
